newsitem.title: UK: CRESTCo seeks support for new settlement regime.
newsitem.headline: CRESTCo seeks support for new settlement regime.

text.p: CRESTCo, the Bank of England-led group developing the Crest computerised share settlement system for the London Stock Exchange, said on Monday it is seeking support of regulators for a rigorous new settlement regime.

An unpublished draft of CRESTCo's new settlement rules dictates that firms using the system will be subject to fines and other sanctions if trades they put into the system are not settled on time, CRESTCo manager Paul Symons told Reuters.
"We're meeting with regulators next month. We need to ensure that a breach of our disciplinary regime is a breach of their rules, as well.
"We need to give our rules as much clout and as many teeth as possible," he added.
CRESTCo's consortium of 60 financial institutions built the system after the exchange's own attempt to develop an electronic system failed.
The London Stock Exchange currently uses a paper-based system, Talisman, to settle most share transactions.

After almost four years under development at a cost of some 29 million stg ($49 million), Crest has experienced software glitches and other problems that have slowed processing times, leading to huge backlogs of unmatched trades since its inauguration in July.
The new heavy-handed rules were designed to eliminate the problems that stem from firms that input information into the system.
"We've made some adjustments to the software, but (performance) also depends upon the way people use the system," Symon said. "It's not always Crest that causes the delays."
CRESTCo also has trained about half a dozen staffers from the London Stock Exchange to help sort out problems, Symon said. "The exchange was very keen to assist us," he added.
He noted that performance has improved during the last couple of months.
"About 79 percent of stocks are settled by their due dates, which is commensurate with Talisman. We still have a long way to go, but it's improving," he said
Two months ago, 60 percent of stocks were settled by their due dates.
Roughly 40 percent of the market is now being settled on Crest. The transition to electronic share settlement from the paper-based system is scheduled to be completed by April 1997.
Yet some settlement managers have expressed concern that the system cannot handle some of the larger volume stocks.

A recent survey conducted by newsletter Securities Interactive showed that 48 percent of the 23 firms polled said they were "unsatisfied" with Crest. Twenty-six percent said they were "quite satisfied," while 22 percent said they were "barely satisfied." Only one firm was "very satisfied" with the operation of Crest so far, the survey said.
